dedupe_keys.name: lights out sea level rise risk to us internet infrastructure 2018

description: This risk assessment estimates how much of the physical internet in the United States will be exposed to sea level rise. The authors overlaid sea level incursion projections from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration on the Internet Atlas map of fibre conduits, points of presence and colocation centres, aligning the data formats and counting the infrastructure under water at intervals over the next 100 years. They found that within 15 years about 4,067 miles of fibre conduit would be under water and 1,101 nodes, such as points of presence and colocation centres, would be surrounded by water. A risk metric combining geographic reach and infrastructure density put the New York, Miami and Seattle areas at highest risk, and among providers CenturyLink, Inteliquent and AT&T. The authors note that buried conduits are designed to be water resistant but not waterproof, and call for mitigation plans and alternative routes. The paper was presented at the Applied Networking Research Workshop in Montreal in July 2018 and was widely reported. Coverage: the contiguous United States, projections to about 2100. Format and access: ACM paper, with a free copy on the author's site; Internet Atlas data are available to researchers. Caveats: sea walls and other defences are not modelled; the Atlas may miss private or unmapped assets. Simulation uses: hazard exposure of telecom, exchange and data-centre assets, climate adaptation planning and network rerouting under loss of coastal links. Related records: the Hurricane Sandy data-centre case shows coastal flooding in practice; CAIDA Ark measures topology.
